chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has two wives, who wishes to prefer one of them with clothing and a gift; is that permissible? He said, 'There is no harm in that, but strive for justice between them.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to give gifts to one wife more than the other in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that preferential treatment in material gifts (kiswa and atiyyah) is permissible without requiring absolute equality, provided the husband exercises sincere effort (ijtihad) to maintain fairness. This ruling distinguishes between the ideal of perfect equity mentioned in the Quran and the practical legal standard of striving for justice, acknowledging human limitations in polygynous marriages. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that 'justice' in gifts allows for discretion rather than rigid mathematical equality.
